claim_field: Each finding carries cause.claim = measured | inferred. 'measured' = seen in the screenshot and, where cited, a source line or HAR entry; 'inferred' = the named cause is not yet checked in code.

source.build_observed: localhost:5174 dev build (address bar in 165743); the running bundle's commit was not recorded. The shared portal working copy read fdccc6e6; origin DEV 1e02be40; PROD 36a37afc.
source.client_walked: a Cottonwood client with two accounts (165515-165932); search on 49financial and Global

outcomes.O1: An advisor types a client's name and the right client is the first thing they see, in a list nothing else on the page covers or competes with.
outcomes.O2: An advisor reads who the client is and which firm it is in, in client language: no account number, token, code or double hyphen in the client's identity.
outcomes.O3: An advisor tells every account of a client apart wherever accounts are listed, and every listed account opens.
outcomes.O4: An advisor reads one account's performance (never a client blend), and when it cannot be shown reads the true reason in plain words, with no control offered that does nothing.
outcomes.O5: An advisor moves from the client total down to one account and its models and back, always seeing where they are, with every percentage labelled with what it is a share of.
outcomes.O6: Every holdings view shows every account of the client.
outcomes.O7: One colour means one thing on the page: no two items in a chart share a colour, and the model palette and the asset-class palette never reuse each other's colours.
outcomes.O8: The page shows client facts on its face and system facts one click away: one navy band, one date format, one money format, no raw codes or system words, no wrapped amounts, no duplicate totals.
outcomes.O9: An advisor reads the securities map: each security once with its total, every tile legible, filters grouped by account.
outcomes.O10: An advisor can trust the holdings figures: they are as of the last trading day, and model amounts are the positions actually held.

findings.observed: The client dropdown opens on an EMPTY query and lists the firm's entries A-Z, acting as a browse list rather than a search.

cause.text: The search list renders results with no query typed.

findings.acceptance: With the search box focused and empty, no result list shows; results appear only for typed text (Browse stays the listing).

findings.observed: The PERFORMANCE tab strip draws ON TOP of the open dropdown, cutting it between the first and second option.

cause.text: Stacking order: the tab strip sits above the dropdown layer.

findings.acceptance: With the dropdown open over the tabs, every option is fully visible and the tab strip is underneath it.

findings.observed: Options are account registrations, not clients: 'A HARE CUST FOR' appears three times with three account tails; every row shows one account's tail and a raw type code ('S1', 'FB').

cause.text: The directory's display_name for many 49F entries is a registration title; the frontend appends the masked discriminator (header/search.ts:94-96 optionLabel).

findings.acceptance: Each option names a client in client language; a client with several registrations appears once; no raw type code in the option.

findings.observed: The firm prints as a token chip ('49financial', 'cottonwood') on every row, inline on some rows and wrapped to its own line on others.

cause.text: The firm token is used as the display name.

findings.acceptance: Every option shows the firm's display name (e.g. 'Cottonwood'), laid out the same on every row.

findings.observed: Behind the dropdown: 'Choose a client to confirm its firm and accounts in Resolution.' uses the system word 'Resolution'.

cause.text: Copy uses an internal term.

findings.acceptance: The empty-state line uses client language only (no 'Resolution').

findings.observed: Before any client is chosen, the Performance area shows a figure ('VS BENCHMARK +2.00%') from the illustrative sample panel.

cause.text: The sample view (tabs/SampleView.tsx) renders under the live page before selection.

findings.acceptance: With no client chosen, the page shows no number that reads like client data.

findings.observed: Typing 'anna thiessen' matches on 'anna' only and lists alphabetically; the real match 'Thiessen, Anna' (Cottonwood) is LAST. Name order differs by firm ('ANNA GARCIA' vs 'Thiessen, Anna') and search does not adjust.

cause.text: No relevance ranking and no name-order normalization; the frontend keeps server order (header/search.ts toOptions has no filter).

findings.acceptance: A full-name query in either order ('anna thiessen', 'thiessen anna') puts the exact client first. The CTO rules whether ranking is server-side (IRPT_BCKEND directory search) or client-side.

findings.observed: The tab strip again covers part of the list: 'ANNA BOROWINSKI' is cut off under it.

findings.observed: 'Performance for this account is temporarily unavailable right now.' is not true for Cottonwood: it needs a one-use Black Diamond plan per account and will not clear by itself. The raw code DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE shows under Details.
